name: Memorial
overview: The biblical concept of memorial centers on God's faithfulness in delivering His people, as seen in the establishment of feasts and ordinances to remember His mighty acts. The Passover is instituted as a perpetual feast to the Lord, serving as a lasting memorial of Israel's deliverance from Egypt (Exodus 12:14). Additionally, the setting apart of the firstborn and the redemption of the firstborn of man and animals underscore a continual remembrance of God's saving power (Exodus 13:12-15). These memorials are not only commemorative but also instructional, prompting future generations to recount God's mighty hand in their history (Exodus 13:14-16).
